By Central Secretariat precedent, aged ministers had once taken part in deliberating major affairs; the practice had long been abandoned. Tiemuertashi memorialized to restore it and appointed Tienhe, Zhang Yuanpu, and four others as deliberative grand councillors.

The emperor said, "Wang Wentong is a rare talent. I only wish I could find someone like him to employ."

unresolvedReferences.description: The packet's reign table covers only Kublai's Zhiyuan (AD 1264–1294). Western years are external conversions verified by web research: Taiding 3 = AD 1326, Zhishun 1 = AD 1330, the later Zhiyuan 4 (under Toghon Temür) = AD 1338, Zhizheng 2 = AD 1342. The 至元四年 of s0029 is read as the later Zhiyuan because Bie'erqiebuhua was only a child under Emperor Wuzong (AD 1307–1311); Kublai's Zhiyuan 4 (AD 1267) is impossible.

Emperors are named by temple name only; identifications and reign dates are external: Xianzong = Möngke (AD 1251–1259; southern campaign AD 1258–1259), Chengzong = Temür (AD 1294–1307), Wuzong = Khaishan (AD 1307–1311), Renzong = Ayurbarwada (AD 1311–1320), Yingzong = Shidebala (AD 1320–1323), Mingzong = Kusala; Empress Dowager Xingsheng = Dagi. Ahuotai's execution (AD 1307) and Mingzong's Yunnan posting (AD 1316) are also external.
天子 (the Son of Heaven) who kept Bie'erqiebuhua at court is not identified; it falls between Yingzong's appointment and Taiding 3 (AD 1320–1326, external).
The unnamed paternal grandfather (between Mangqietu and Ahuotai) is entailed by 曾祖 and carries a research hold; the unnamed mother is entailed by 丁內艱 (s0021).
賢帥 ('our former worthy commander') refers to an unnamed forebear who held the hereditary Baban post; too indefinite to register as a person.

Bare years 四年, 七年 and 十年 in Bie'erqiebuhua's biography and 四年, 五年 in Taiping's are read as Zhizheng, continuing from 至正二年 (s0030, s0064); Western years are external conversions (Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341; Yuantong 1333–1335), verified by web research.
帝 (the emperor) in the Zhizheng-era narrative is identified as Emperor Shundi (Toghon Temür), named in s0060, by external chronology.
Bie'erqiebuhua's son 達世帖木而 (Dashitiemuer) is kept distinct from the chapter-title subject 達識帖睦邇, whom the packet also romanises Dashitiemuer; the characters differ.

External reign dates: Emperor Taiding AD 1323–1328, Emperor Wenzong AD 1328–1332; Zhao Mengfu died AD 1322 (external research); the completion of the Liao, Jin and Song histories is dated AD 1343–1345 by external research.
Renjie and Sheng are given names only; the surname He is implied by Taiping's original surname 賀. Renjie carries a research hold (no date).
Bare years 六年 to 十六年 are read as Zhizheng, continuing from earlier units; Western years are external conversions (Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341), verified by web research.
帝 (the emperor) is identified as Emperor Shundi by external chronology. 先臣 in Duo'erzhi's speech is taken as his late father (strongly inferred); it could be a more distant forebear.

The Toqto'a episode is a flashback bounded by narrative order before Zhizheng 9 (AD 1349); external research dates Toqto'a's dismissal to AD 1344, Majaritai's death to AD 1347 and Toqto'a's return as Grand Tutor to AD 1349.
The imperial-clan woman Yexianhudou married, or was to marry, is recorded as his spouse with uncertain relationship state; the text says only that he 'should not presumptuously marry' her.
Toqto'a's brothers are an undifferentiated plural and are preserved as a family summary rather than as people.

Bare years 十七年 to 二十七年 are read as Zhizheng; Western years are external conversions (Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341), verified by web research. Events between dated entries are bounded by narrative order; external research dates Zhang Shicheng's surrender to AD 1357, Aluhui Temür's rising to AD 1361 and Taiping's death to AD 1363.

Identifications from outside the text: 帝 = Emperor Shundi (Toghon Temür); 二皇后奇氏 = Empress Gi (Qi), of Korean origin; 皇太子 = Ayushiridara. The chapter states no parentage for the Crown Prince, so no family edge is recorded.
Two different men are romanised 'Puhua' in the English: the eunuch 樸不花 (Pu Buhua, s0116) and Censor-in-Chief 普化 (s0134); they are kept as separate people.
The English spells Taiping's son 'Yexianhudu' here and 'Yexianhudou' earlier; both render 也先忽都 and refer to the same man.
Taiping's birth year (c. AD 1301) is a computation from his age at death (63 sui) and the externally dated death year of AD 1363; not stated in the text.

Yexianhudou's dismissal is dated AD 1349 by cross-reference to Taiping's Zhizheng 9 demotion (s0092); 'after six years' (s0144) gives c. AD 1355. Western years are external conversions (Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341; the later Zhiyuan 1 = AD 1335), verified by web research. 後至元 in s0166 explicitly marks the later Zhiyuan, so the packet's Kublai-era Zhiyuan table does not apply.
Choson's great case and Yexianhudou's death carry no year; they are bounded between Zhizheng 19 (AD 1359) and the fall of the Yuan capital in AD 1368 (external).
The Toghan tortured in the great case may be the Toghan who was Yexianhudou's former officer (s0128), but the text does not say so; kept as a separate person here.

Prince (國王) Toqto'a, Tiemuertashi's father, is distinct from the councillor Toqto'a of s0086–s0093. Identifications from outside the text: 帝/天子 = Emperor Shundi; 皇太子 = Ayushiridara; Mingzong = Kusala; Wenzong = Tugh Temür; Bayan's fall dated AD 1340 by external research.
Yexianhudou's mother is entailed by 丁內艱; the text does not say she was Taiping's principal wife, so no spouse edge is recorded.

Bare years 五年 and 七年 are read as Zhizheng; Western years are external conversions (Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341), verified by web research. Tiemuertashi's death is bounded within half a year of his AD 1347 appointment (external research: AD 1347); his birth c. AD 1302 is a computation from his age of 46.
帝 is identified as Emperor Shundi by external chronology. 爾先人 ('your forebear') is taken as Tiemuertashi's father, Prince Toqto'a of s0162 (strongly inferred).

Recalled figures carry only their own life dates: Confucius 551–479 BC (external); Emperor Shizu = Kublai, per the packet's reign table (Zhiyuan AD 1264–1294; accession AD 1260 external); Wang Wentong executed AD 1262 (external); Yao and Shun are legendary. The dates of the conversation go only on retrospective-reference claims.
Bayan's abolition of the examinations is dated AD 1335 by external research; the text says only 'earlier'.
Dashitiemuer (達識帖睦邇) appears in this chunk only as the undated heading of his biography.

Bare years 九年 to 十九年 are read as Zhizheng; Western years are external conversions (Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341), verified by web research. External research dates Fang Guozhen's rising to AD 1348 (the text has Zhizheng 11), Yang Wanzhe's death to AD 1358 and Zhang Shicheng's proclamation as Prince of Wu to AD 1363.
Shixin (士信) is listed right after 其弟士德 ('his younger brother Shide'); the sibling edge to Zhang Shicheng is strongly inferred, and external history confirms him as Zhang Shixin, Shicheng's brother.

The English garbles two names: 普賢奴 (Puxiannu, rendered 'Pu Huatieer') and 楊完者 (Yang Wanzhe, rendered 'Waner'). Only the first is repaired; 'Waner' recurs in about twenty units and is recorded through the person label and pinyin.
Yang Wanzhe's brother Bayan (伯顏) is distinct from the councillor Bayan of s0168 and s0212.

Bare 二十四年 is read as Zhizheng 24 = AD 1364 (external conversion, Zhizheng 1 = AD 1341, web-verified). External research dates Zhang Shicheng's proclamation as Prince of Wu to AD 1363, the deaths of Puhua Timur and Dashitiemuer to AD 1364, and Puhua Timur's Fujian post to AD 1358.
Puhua Timur (普化帖木兒) may be the same man as a 'Puhua' mentioned in earlier chunks; no identity is asserted here.
大夫 ('the Censor-in-Chief') refers back to Puhua Timur, who had just died.
